correctness.rationale: Comparing two deletion outputs reduces equality to agreement of all intervening lag-k pairs, so deletion-position classes are intervals and the number of distinct outputs is one plus the mismatch count. Vertex spins give independent edge signs on a forest and pairwise independence on any simple graph, proving the binomial marginals and zero covariance. At L=b+c the map v↦v+b mod L traces each undirected edge once (the return-in-two-steps case would require b=c), forming gcd(b,c) cycles. Each residue-r cycle has largest vertex L-g+r, c/g b-edges, and b/g c-edges; restricting to an initial segment leaves a forest through L-g and exactly one cycle at L-g+1. Above that threshold, the first cycle persists, and the fair-spin PGF expansion has a strictly positive even-subgraph term on 0<z,u<1, so independence fails at every larger length. At the critical length only the empty set and the full cycle have even degrees, giving precisely the two printed terms; residual exponents count edges outside the cycle. Independent direct-string tests covered lengths 3–10, 120 triples and 59,384 word/parameter cases, with exact critical PGF comparisons at 22 triples and graph-rank checks in 70 cases.
